data.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/llm/config.py` is at the janitor cap edge because `LLMConfig.from_env` still owns the table-driven parsing for model/provider, budgets, tracing, web, and path settings. The parent story already fixed the intended boundary: keep `LLMConfig.from_env` as the only precedence/composition facade while moving those reader clusters into a focused sibling leaf.

## Approach

Extract the existing table-driven reader logic into `src/rebar/llm/config_readers.py` (or focused siblings if the current leaf already exists) so model/provider, budget, tracing, web, and path parsing are owned outside `LLMConfig.from_env`. Preserve the exact current defaults, validation errors, environment/config precedence, and monkeypatch-visible import surface while shrinking the facade's body.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/config.py`
- `src/rebar/llm/config_readers.py`
- `tests/unit/test_config_llm.py`
- `tests/unit/test_llm_config_pointer.py`
- `tests/unit/test_llm_config_gate_root.py`

## Testing

Run focused config precedence/default/error tests that cover config-file, environment, explicit override, malformed value, missing value, and cross-field precedence, plus lint/typecheck/module-size gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Table-driven readers for model/provider, budgets, tracing, web, and path settings move out of `LLMConfig.from_env` without duplicating precedence logic.
- [ ] `LLMConfig.from_env` remains the sole precedence/composition facade.
- [ ] Existing defaults, validation failures, environment/config precedence, and monkeypatch-visible behavior remain value-equivalent.
- [ ] Focused config tests plus lint, typecheck, module-size, and complexity gates pass.
data.title: Extract table-driven LLM config readers
